transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-07 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Romano (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (BeaconRx CTO), Evan Torres (BeaconRx ML Eng), Priya Singh (BeaconRx Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): walked through Optimize scorecard for selecting quantization profiles; demoed console scorecard and how to interpret fidelity vs latency deltas; discussed rollout runbook including canaries and fallback to FP16; agreed on sandbox + bench.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Maya from Redwood, our SE Luca is here as well. How's BeaconRx doing?
[00:06] Aisha: Good, thanks. Lots of things, but this is the call we wanted — the team wants to understand how to pick quant profiles without breaking the clinical flows.
[00:12] Maya: Totally understood. Today we'll walk the Optimize scorecard playbook — sort of a step-by-step: pick profiles, run sensitivity, review the scorecard (latency, cost, QA delta), then rollout with canaries and fallbacks.
[00:22] Evan: Quick note on our side: latency targets are pretty tight for triage suggestions, aiming for <220ms p99. Token costs are still important but SLA first.
[00:30] Luca: Good, we'll keep that top of mind. Quick housekeeping — I'm going to demo the Optimize console and then show a small bench we ran earlier. The demo uses a sample clinical prompt set so you'll see realistic deltas, but we want your corpus for the final bench.
[00:42] Priya: Sounds good. Also curious about how much work for our infra team if we go dedicated or private later.

[01:00] Luca: Starting the console — apologies if the naming's a little off in the auto captions, sometimes it shows 'Op-timize' as two words, Ugh. Here is the scorecard. Columns: baseline FP16 (we use FP16 as the control), INT8 profile A, FP8 profile B. Rows: latency p50/p90/p99, avg tokens/sec, per-token cost, QA delta (BLEU/ROUGE-style or custom eval), and stability score (how often outputs deviate).
[01:25] Maya: Important to call out: FP8 often gives better latency than FP16 in our runtime because it reduces memory footprint and improves kernel utilization, but quality delta varies with model family and prompt distribution. INT8 is more aggressive and sometimes needs mixed precision fallback or additional calibration.
[01:40] Aisha: When you say 'calibration' do you mean extra retraining or just tuning the quant profile?
[01:45] Luca: Mostly tuning — collecting representative tokens for quant statistics and running a sweep. Rarely do you have to fine-tune the model; that's usually only if you see systematic hallucinations.
[01:55] Evan: Are these sweeps automated in Optimize or do we provide scripts?
[01:58] Luca: Optimize has a guided sweep flow. You upload prompts, it runs profiles in parallel across the sandbox, captures latency and scoring, and outputs the scorecard. We also emit examples where outputs diverge so you can do spot checks.

[02:15] Maya: Let's look at an example scorecard from a health sandbox we ran. Baseline p99 = 210ms, INT8 p99 = 160ms, FP8 p99 = 170ms; cost per 1k tokens reduced by 48% (INT8) and 42% (FP8) respectively. QA delta — small for FP8 (~1.2% drop on our clinical summary metric), bigger for INT8 (~3.8% drop) on that workload.
[02:40] Priya: Interesting. That aligns with what we feared — INT8 gives better savings but more quality risk. How do we quantify acceptable QA delta?
[02:48] Maya: We recommend building a scorecard threshold matrix up front. For example: if QA delta <1.5% and latency improvement >20% pick FP8; if QA delta <4% and latency improvement >30% you might consider INT8 with canary. But that's just a starting point, and you should weight false positives differently based on downstream risk.
[03:05] Aisha: For triage we can't accept a 4% drop. For non-critical suggestions maybe.
[03:10] Evan: We can split endpoints: triage stays FP16/FP8 conservative, follow-ups can be INT8. Is routing supported?
[03:15] Luca: Yes — routing rules in the runtime allow per-route model variants. You can set a route to use an INT8 flavor for low-risk calls and FP16/FP8 for high-risk ones. Canary percentages and auto-fallback are configurable.
[03:25] Maya: Also the KV cache behavior matters — small changes in quantization can affect token generation speed differently depending on prompt prefixing. Our console sim shows prefix-related cache hits and how they affect effective latency.

[03:40] Evan: A question on the bench: you mentioned stability score. How is that computed?
[03:44] Luca: It's a composite: fraction of responses that match baseline semantics per our eval set, plus n-gram overlap metrics and a human flag probability metric we estimate from our regression models. So it's not perfect but gives a quick triage.
[03:55] Priya: Can we plug in our internal human eval labels? We have a small team that grades outputs.
[03:59] Luca: Absolutely. Optimize allows you to upload human labels and use them to compute true error rates. The scorecard will then show a 'human-aligned delta' column.

[04:20] Aisha: Security questions — we need SOC2 compliance, KMS integration, and logs for auditors. If we do a pilot in your hosted environment, what audit artifacts do we get?
[04:30] Maya: For hosted pilots we provide SOC2 summary, audit logs for request/response metadata (not full PII unless you enable it), and you can opt into customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. We also have VPC peering for private deployments. For BeaconRx we normally suggest an initial hosted sandbox with strict token redaction and then a Dedicated pilot if audit needs are higher.
[04:49] Aisha: Good. Data residency: can we restrict to eu-west-1?
[04:53] Maya: Yes, we can pin the sandbox region. For production Dedicated or Private, you can also host on-prem.

[05:05] Evan: Back to model fidelity — if we pick INT8 for a subset and then see regressions in production, what's the rollback path?
[05:10] Luca: You can set a fallback rule: if error rate or regression metric exceeds threshold for X minutes, route automatically falls back to baseline FP16. We also recommend canary at 5% for 48 hours with active monitoring.
[05:20] Priya: What about cost math — can we see token-level cost per route?
[05:23] Maya: Yes — Console gives token-level breakdown and per-route spend estimates. Optimize will project monthly savings given your usage pattern.

[05:35] Luca: I'm going to share a short handoff CSV we produced for a medical triage demo — it contains latency rows and sample outputs. Note the transcription here sometimes says 'K-B cache' — that's supposed to be KV cache. Sorry about the auto captions.
[05:50] Aisha: Haha, no worries.
[06:00] [Demonstration noise — screen share walkthrough of console scorecard for 8 minutes]
[14:10] Luca: Back from the demo. A few gotchas to call out: 1) INT8 sensitivity varies a lot with token distribution; for short prompts you'll often see bigger percent changes. 2) FP8 profiles are newer; for some model shards we still tune kernels. 3) Mixed-precision fallback is your safety valve.
[14:30] Evan: For our short triage prompts — 20 to 60 tokens — does that mean INT8 risk is amplified?
[14:35] Luca: Yes, shorter sequences mean the per-token noise can have a larger proportional effect on small outputs. FP8 sometimes gives steadier results for short prompts.
[14:45] Maya: Also worth describing rollout cadence: run a sandbox sweep -> choose candidate profile(s) -> run an internal A/B (canary) on a percentage -> human-in-the-loop checks on flagged divergences -> full rollout.
[14:58] Priya: How many prompts do you usually need for a robust sweep?
[15:02] Luca: We recommend 300–1,000 representative prompts; for high-stakes clinical flows aim for closer to 1k plus a human review set of 200 edge cases.
[15:12] Aisha: We can do 500 initial prompts. Evan will share.
[15:15] Evan: Yep, I'll extract 500 later today.

[15:22] Maya: Quick note on metrics: don't over-index on n-gram overlap; semantic tests and task-specific metrics are better. Our Optimize supports custom evaluation functions — you can plug your triage accuracy metric in.
[15:35] Aisha: That helps. On the legal side, MSA — do you have a pilot addendum?
[15:40] Maya: Yes, we'll share a pilot MSA and an entry-level security pack.

[15:50] Priya: For the bench results you showed earlier, there were some examples where INT8 changed a medication name. That would be unacceptable for us. How do we catch that?
[15:58] Luca: We have targeted validators — you can configure entities that must be preserved (medication names, dosages). The bench flags any outputs where an entity mismatch is detected. Those cases get put into the 'blocker' bucket and cause auto-fail for that profile unless manually approved.
[16:15] Priya: Great.

[16:20] Aisha: Timeframe question — if we like the sandbox results, how soon could we start a pilot?
[16:24] Maya: We can spin a sandbox in 2–3 business days. Dedicated pilot depends on capacity and procurement; typically 4–6 weeks once contracts are signed.
[16:34] Evan: Is there a lab we can run to simulate p99 under load?
[16:38] Luca: Yes, we have a benchmark harness that drives realistic traffic and captures p50/p90/p99. We'll run it for you on the profiles you pick and provide the CSV.

[16:48] Maya: I'm going to read the agreed next steps so we all have alignment. 1) BeaconRx to provide 500 prompts and latency SLOs by 2025-11-09. 2) Redwood to provision Optimize sandbox and invite the team by 2025-11-10. 3) Redwood to run initial INT8 vs FP8 bench and return results by 2025-11-14. 4) Schedule a benchmarking call week of 2025-11-17.
[17:10] Aisha: That works. One more: can we get a sample of the security pack and SOC2 summary?
[17:14] Maya: Yes — I'll attach that in the follow-up email.

[17:20] Evan: About billing — if we do a pilot, is usage billed or covered by credits?
[17:24] Maya: For initial pilots we normally provide credits for sandbox usage; for a dedicated pilot we'd discuss a committed pilot cost. We'll include details in the pricing template.

[17:35] Priya: On the UI, is there an API flow if we want to automate profile rollouts?
[17:40] Luca: Yes, everything in Console is backed by an API — you can script rollouts, fallback rules, and pull scorecards programmatically.

[17:50] [short pause, light cross-talk about calendars]
[18:05] Maya: Anything else from BeaconRx?
[18:08] Aisha: I think that's it for now; excited to see the bench.
[18:12] Evan: Same. We'll get the prompts over by EOD.
[18:15] Priya: I'll coordinate on product acceptance criteria and share a doc link.

[18:20] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the sandbox link, pricing template, the pilot MSA, and the SOC2/security pack. Luca will run the bench and share the CSV.
[18:30] Luca: Thanks everyone.
[18:32] Meeting end.
